summary: Sustained throughput degradation from prefetch pipeline lock + heterogeneous GPU placement failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using a dedicated pool in us-west reported a sustained drop in throughput (p50 throughput down ~40%, p99 latency increased ~3x) that began around 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. This started shortly after the customer pinned a new model variant and then executed a large concurrent embeddings job from a third-party tenant.

Impact:
- Acme Retail experienced degraded real-time inference for checkout fraud scoring (ML path) for ~2.5 hours, impacting ~8% of calls to the dedicated pool and causing backpressure to downstream systems.
- Observed increased allocation failures and pending-attach times for GPU slots; autoscaler triggered scale-ups but GPU attach times remained high.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-usw-3 (mixed GPU types: A100 (40GB) + H100 (80GB) nodes), scheduling policy: balanced-affinity, autoscaler: predictive with 30s cooldown.
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-2).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Customer pinned redwood-compat-7b to a dedicated pool route and began a scheduled model migration at 09:10 UTC.
2) Concurrently another tenant (unknown at first) started a high-concurrency embeddings sweep from the same pool.
3) Within ~2 minutes, p50 throughput for pinned route fell and p99 latency increased with many requests showing "pending-attach" states and repeated allocation retries.

Observed logs & metrics (selected):
- allocator.log: repeated messages "slot: pending attach timeout=65s" and "attach failed: nvlink peer error".
- autoscaler metrics: several scale-out events logged but new nodes reported long attach times (avg 45s) and failed prefetch rate increased.
- runtime telemetry: spike in PCIe / NVLink utilization on some H100 hosts, elevated GPU memory churn and prefetch eviction counts.
- network: no cluster-wide network outage; control-plane healthy.

Hypothesis: heterogeneous GPU mix combined with a high-IO embeddings job caused NVLink/PCIe saturation and prefetch buffer thrashing. The allocator detected failed placement attempts (peer NVLink errors) and started preempting smaller slot allocations, which increased slot fragmentation and left many requests in pending-attach while autoscaler spun up new, but slow-to-attach, nodes. A noisy-tenant embeddings sweep amplified I/O noise and caused thermal/driver retries on a subset of H100 nodes which cascaded into allocation churn.

Immediate impact mitigation requested by customer: reduce p99 latency and restore p50 throughput for pinned route.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:18 UTC: Support engaged SRE after initial triage; collected allocator, autoscaler, and runtime traces.
Found that 6/24 nodes in dp-usw-3 were H100 and reported elevated nvlink errors starting at 09:11 UTC.
Prefetch eviction rate increased 8x in the affected hosts; KV cache growth observed with concurrent small-stream fanout from embeddings job.
Autoscaler behavior: predictive scale-up triggered but new nodes remained in 'attaching' for 30-60s; multiple attach failures retried, increasing pending queue.
Investigated GitHub PR history: recent sidecar update PR#8421 modified snapshot flush cadence and may increase NVMe IO during high-concurrency workloads.
Cross-checked with monitoring: no control-plane CPU or etcd errors; kernel driver logs on affected hosts show NVLink retry messages consistent with heavy PCIe/NVLink traffic.
comments: Support (Anita Patel) - 2026-03-10 09:25 UTC: We're seeing pending-attach spikes and NVLink errors in allocator logs. Asking customer to temporarily route traffic to an alternate pool if possible.
Customer (Acme SRE - Jordan Lee) - 2026-03-10 09:32 UTC: We can divert non-critical batch embeddings off this pool; doing so now and will report if throughput recovers.
SRE (Marco Ruiz) - 2026-03-10 09:45 UTC: We're isolating nodes reporting NVLink errors and cordoning them from the pool; forcing a small rolling restart of the sidecars on affected hosts.

Engineering (Priya Menon) - 2026-03-10 10:10 UTC: Observed that sidecar snapshot flusher aligns with embeddings sweep causing IO bursts. Created a temporary rate-limit on snapshot flush in PR#8421 (hotfix branch) for further testing.
Support (Anita Patel) - 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC: Customer reports p50 throughput improved from -40% to -12% after divert and cordon; p99 still elevated. Continuing investigation.
root_cause: Mixed GPU pool where H100 hosts experienced NVLink/PCIe saturation due to concurrent high-throughput embeddings job from a noisy tenant plus a sidecar snapshot flush cadence that aligned with the sweep. This caused attach failures and allocator retries, resulting in slot fragmentation and prolonged pending-attach times while autoscaler attempted to add capacity.
resolution: Applied immediate mitigations: cordoned 4 H100 hosts showing repeated NVLink errors; applied temporary sidecar snapshot-rate limit; asked customer to route non-critical batch embeddings to a different pool. After mitigations p50 throughput recovered to within 90% of baseline and p99 latency decreased but not fully to baseline. Engineering prepared a code change (hotfix PR) to stagger snapshot flush and add NVLink attach retry backoff tweaks.
workaround: 1) Customers on affected pool can temporarily divert heavy batch/embeddings jobs to alternate dedicated pool or to hosted API. 2) We cordoned noisy nodes and restarted sidecars which reduces immediate IO contention. 3) If model pinning is in use, consider rolling migration windows to avoid coupling with tenant batch windows.
next_steps: Merge and roll hotfix PR to stagger snapshot flush and adjust attach backoff (PR#8421-hotfix).
Schedule a capacity-tiering recommendation for Acme: move latency-sensitive routes to homogeneous H100-only pool or tag H100/A100 separately.
Add autoscaler detection for sustained NVLink attach errors as a signal to prefer homogeneous placements or avoid predictive scale-up into heterogeneous hosts.
Postmortem to be created and linked to this ticket with timeline and monitoring runbooks for noisy-tenant detection.
resolution_status: Partial mitigation applied; hotfix planned and awaiting deployment
customer_impact_summary: Acme Retail saw degraded inference throughput for latency-sensitive routes affecting checkout scoring; business impact limited by fallback routes but required SRE support during peak window.
